lines.text: How does this cell leave your blood? This wall has no open door.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ dˈʌz ðɪs sˈɛl lˈiːv jɔː blˈʌd? ðɪs wˈɔːl hɐz nˈəʊ ˈəʊpən dˈɔː.

lines.text: It's a neutrophil, the most common white cell in adults, about as wide as a red one. Under a sore fingertip, they pile up outside the wall.
lines.phonemes: ɪts ɐ njˈuːtɹəfˌɪl, ðə mˈəʊst kˈɒmən wˈaɪt sˈɛl ɪn ˈadʌlts, ɐbˌaʊt az wˈaɪd az ɐ ɹˈɛd wˌɒn. ˌʌndəɹ ɐ sˈɔː fˈɪŋɡətˌɪp, ðeɪ pˈaɪl ˌʌp aʊtsˈaɪd ðə wˈɔːl.

lines.text: Rudolf Virchow taught that pus grew from the inflamed tissue. In eighteen sixty-seven, his assistant Julius Cohnheim watched a living frog's vessels. White cells climbed out.
lines.phonemes: ɹˈuːdɒlf fˈɪəkəʊ tˈɔːt ðat pˈʌs ɡɹˈuː fɹʌmðɪ ɪnflˈeɪmd tˈɪʃuː. ɪn ˈeɪtiːn sˈɪkstisˈɛvən, hɪz ɐsˈɪstənt dʒˈuːlɪəs kˈəʊnhaɪm wˈɒtʃt ɐ lˈɪvɪŋ fɹˈɒɡz vˈɛsəlz. wˈaɪt sˈɛlz klˈaɪmd ˈaʊt.

lines.text: Where you're hurt or infected, the wall turns sticky, and the cell rolls. Then its grips switch on, and it stops. In mice, it crawls to a seam in the wall. In a rare inherited condition, those grips are faulty. Cells roll on past.
lines.phonemes: wˌeə jɔː hˈɜːt ɔːɹ ɪnfˈɛktɪd, ðə wˈɔːl tˈɜːnz stˈɪki, and ðə sˈɛl ɹˈəʊlz. ðˈɛn ɪts ɡɹˈɪps swˈɪtʃ ˈɒn, and ɪt stˈɒps. ɪn mˈaɪs, ɪt kɹˈɔːlz tʊ ɐ sˈiːm ɪnðə wˈɔːl. ɪn ɐ ɹˈeəɹ ɪnhˈɛɹɪtɪd kəndˈɪʃən, ðəʊz ɡɹˈɪps ɑː fˈɒlti. sˈɛlz ɹˈəʊl ˈɒn pˈɑːst .

lines.text: This one wedges its nucleus into the seam, making its own door. It pours through a gap narrower than itself. In lab studies, the seam seals shut behind it.
lines.phonemes: ðˈɪswˌɒn wˈɛdʒɪz ɪts njˈuːklɪəs ˌɪntʊ ðə sˈiːm, mˌeɪkɪŋ ɪts ˈəʊn dˈɔː. ɪt pˈɔːz θɹuː ɐ ɡˈap nˈaɹəʊə ðɐn ɪtsˈɛlf. ɪn lˈab stˈʌdiz, ðə sˈiːm sˈiːlz ʃˈʌt bɪhˈaɪnd ɪt.

lines.text: So pus is mostly white cells from your blood. In mice, white cells open their own way out.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ pˈʌs ɪz mˈəʊstli wˈaɪt sˈɛlz fɹɒm jɔː blˈʌd. ɪn mˈaɪs, wˈaɪt sˈɛlz ˈəʊpən ðeəɹ ˈəʊn wˈeɪ ˈaʊt.

lines.text: Meanwhile, as you watched, your bones made more than ten million new ones.
lines.phonemes: mˈiːnwaɪl, az juː wˈɒtʃt, jɔː bˈəʊnz mˌeɪd mˈɔː ðɐn tˈɛn mˈɪliən njˈuː wˌɒnz.

lines.text: Next: season two. What sets off nearly every heartbeat?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: sˈiːzən tˈuː. wˌɒt sˈɛts ˈɒf nˌiəli ˈɛvɹɪ hˈɑːtbiːt?
